channel.title: Concept : Ever Burning Flames.
channel.description: Posts in the discussion thread "Concept : Ever Burning Flames." - A Flame that can't be put out. It will burn a entire city and be found by the SCP foundation.

item.title: Re: Concept : Ever Burning Flames.
item.content:encoded:
So essentially its like amaterasu that can be used with the Mangekyō Sharingan from naruto, right? But green.

He and his family escaped there apartment as the fire was spreading. Then, it shows there experience about being in a zone of infinite place.

I really don't understand the part that you talk about the "infinite place". They were in the apartment and them they escape? The "infinite place" is an anomaly linked to the green flames?

I think you should try adding more original elements to the narrative, and that could even explain how the guy escapes. You have to tie that two points for that to work. And how the Foundation was able to countain it? You could use that in your story too.

Maybe instead of just fire, it could be a sensient anomaly. Its alive and when it burns something its eating it. It could sustain itself only with living organisms. The citys remais intact, but the people are vurned alive. And if the Foundation was able to countain it, the SCP could pose a question to the ethics comitee: should they feed the fire and avoid it to breakout?

I think you could improve a lot your idea!

Have a great day!

:D

item.title: Re: Concept : Ever Burning Flames.
item.content:encoded:
1) If the flames continue to grow then why would they stop at the edge of the city? Especially considering that there are actually more burnables there than in the center of the city? Also, how was it contained? There just seem a lot of things that are ill-defined here, and they should be better defined.

2) Speaking of: The zone of infinite place needs to be better defined. It just feels like it was added to justify the survival of the survivor and the book. If it's going to be part of the SCP, then it needs to be reasonably well-defined.

3) The bottom lines is that you've thrown so much stuff into the SCP without really defining anything that there's just nothing for a reader to grab on to, from the gauntlet to the infinite space, and the overall feel is that you're just throwing stuff at a wall hoping something will stick. Slow down, think it through, and focus on what needs to happen. Just focus on what it needs and see what happens.

item.title: Re: Concept : Ever Burning Flames.
item.content:encoded:
+ Cope Crit
- Close

Okay, let's see what we have…

The core idea is that the flames are made out of something else and a meteor had landed into a building in a city in China. The flames were green. The flames could burn down anything after they had tested it. It then spreads to a entire city. Then, the foundation notices it hasn't been stopped. The meteor that landed, had a gauntlet of the green flame after being collected by the foundation. There was a drawing of meteor dropping and a city burning. The zone that was burning was contained.

So, just for me to restate; This is a green fire that never can be extinguished or stop growing. The ideas alone is kinda boring. Is there anything else to it?

A journal about a person that was trapped in the zone that was being flamed. He and his family escaped there apartment as the fire was spreading. Then, it shows there experience about being in a zone of infinite place. The person who was writing it, eventually dies from starvation. The notebook was found near the border. The fire already has spread to the entire city so most of the information was burned.

A journal of survivors certainly can give a good narrative. But why should I be excited for a survivor in a burning fire? Also, what's the "infinite place". How did the notebook get to the border and why would the Foundation be interested in one burning book from presumably thousands of burning items?

Overall Thoughts: The idea is rather boring and I don't quiet understand how the Foundation would obtain the journal. I would suggest having a source to the anomaly and have a series of logs with a MTF attempting to contain the anomaly.

- Close
